sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04.11.2023 at about 4.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EU- 8966 from BM Road, carefully, by following all the traffic rules.

When he reached infront of HP Petrol Bunk, Pepsi gate BM road, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South, at that time an auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-AJ-2979, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, Kengeri and thereafter he was shifted to Bharath Kempanna Health Care Hospital, B.M.
Road, Bidadi, Ramanagara District, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was doing Fabrication work and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kumbalagudu Police have registered the case against the driver of the said auto-rickshaw, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, he is the owner of the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AJ-2979 and it was insured with the respondent No.2, vide Policy No.140522323390001948, valid from 28.03.2023 to 27.03.2024 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

He has denied the age,
income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by petitioner.

sentences.text: Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 04.11.2023 at about 4.00 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EU- 8966, from BM road,

carefully, by following all the traffic rules and reached infront of HP Petrol Bunk, Pepsi gate BM road, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South, at that time the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AJ- 2979, drove the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was doing Fabrication work and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing his examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 14 documents as Ex.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot-mahazar, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of notice u/s 133 of M.V.Act, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of reply to said notice, Ex.P.8 is certified copy of MVA Report,
Ex.P.9 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.10 is Discharge summary, Ex.P.11 are medical bills (30 in nos.), Ex.P.12 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.13 is OPD Book and Ex.P.14 is X- ray.

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 9, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AJ-2979 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries to his left leg.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.9, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AJ-2979 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injury to his left leg in the said accident.

13. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AJ- 2979 in the alleged accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and they taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner himself and there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ-2979.
But, the respondent No.1 and 2 have failed to establish the said contentions.
The respondents have neither adduced any oral evidence, nor they have produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even they have not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

If really the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner and there was no fault on the part of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw, the same could have been easily established by the respondents by examining the eye-witness to the alleged Channabasavaraja Deshamukh vs Murthy B H on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170329090/
4 accident.

sentences.text: But, the respondents have not taken any strain to examine the eye- witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to them.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no corroborative oral or documentary evidence on record, which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner himself.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ-2979 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to his left leg in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 28 feet wide Bengaluru-Mysore road, infront of HP Petrol Bunk, near Pepsi gate,
Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South, in between the offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ- 2979 and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EU-8966 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.8, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ-2979.
On the other hand, the respondents have not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false or concocted documents.

Further,
the investigation officer in his Ex.P.9 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ-2979 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injury to his left leg in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date,
time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 OPD Book and Ex.P.14 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has suffered Left Tibial Shaft comminuted fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02- AJ-2979 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

19. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ-2979 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained Left Tibial Shaft comminuted fracture and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
As per Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 21.05.2002.
The accident has taken place on 04.11.2023 at about 4.00 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 21 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered Left Tibia Shaft comminuted fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, there is 28% physical disability of left lower limb and 14% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge Channabasavaraja Deshamukh vs Murthy B H on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170329090/
6 summary, Ex.P.13 OPD Book and Ex.P.14 X-Ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injury and he has undergone surgery for the said injury.

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his evidence that, the fracture is united and he has not mentioned the formula on the basis of which he has assessed the disability of the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was doing Fabrication work and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondents have specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same, he has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in the year 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,92,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 21 years is 18.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,92,000 X 10/100 X 18 = Rs.3,45,600/-.

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.

All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.1,26,692/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,26,692/- under the head of medical expenses.

sentences.text: In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury to his left leg i.e. Left Tibia Shaft comminuted fracture.
As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days from 05.11.2023 to 07.11.2023, in Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Bidadi, Ramanagara.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days in Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Bidadi, Ramanagara.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 3 = Rs.3,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days from 05.11.2023 to 07.11.2023, in Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Bidadi,
Ramanagara.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 3 = Rs.2,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Muddebihal, Yarazri Taluk, Vijayapura,
the accident has taken place on Bengaluru-Mysore road, infront of HP Petrol Bunk, Pepsi gate,
Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru city and the petitioner has taken treatment at Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Bidadi, Ramanagara.
Taking into consideration the distance in between place of accident and place of treatment, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 3 days as in-patient at Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Bidadi, Ramanagara, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 1 months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.16,000 x 1 = Rs.16,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 21 years and unfortunately he has suffered Left Tibia Shaft comminuted fracture.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not stated anything about the cost of said surgery and even he has not issued estimation of cost for said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,88,692/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AJ- 2979.
The insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.140522323390001948, in respect of offending Auto was valid from 28.03.2023 to 27.03.2024.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e., 04.11.2023.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of said policy.

The R.W.1 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, as per the document marked as Ex.R.2, the offending auto- rickshaw bearing No.
KA-02-AJ-2979 was having valid permit from 18-04-2023 to 17-04-2028 and it was valid on the date of accident.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AJ-2979 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,88,692/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and they taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner himself and there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ-2979.
If really the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner and there was no fault on the part of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw, the same could have been easily established by the respondents by examining the eye-witness to the alleged Channabasavaraja Deshamukh vs Murthy B H on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170329090/
4 accident.
But, the respondents have not taken any strain to examine the eye- witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to them.
In such circumstances, there is absolutely no corroborative oral or documentary evidence on record, which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner himself.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02-AJ-2979.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date,
time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-02- AJ-2979 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same, he has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The accident took place in the year 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,92,000/-.
